meta.forward_rule: A ROLLING RE-PLAN from a LIVE opening. Only the opening is observed; every day after today is computed. Nothing past today has happened.
meta.pieces_booked_today_basis: booked_today is goods receipts into BH-PF dated today. The receipt date lags the production date by 0-1 day and varies by SKU — this is production BOOKED, not 'produced today'.
meta.pieces_made_mtd_basis: NOT NETTED OFF THE PLAN on this run. The pieces per item code for every day already gone this month now arrive with factory_history (out["history"]) and are published as records; reducing the plan by them changes what the engine is asked to make, so it is a deliberate next step, not a side effect of reading them. Published as null rather than as a figure the plan beside it does not use. The engine does not read this field.

totals.oil_changes_basis: not worked out on this run — it needs the machine-by-machine running order

plan.source: the month's target, carried from the last plan — it is not re-read every cycle

demand.note: what customers want mixes confirmed orders with expected orders — this month's target, not ordered yet. Expected rows are marked in the data and must always look different on the page

opening.oil_l_definition: all oil in the tanks right now, every kind — the day pages count only the oils in this month's recipes, so the two are not the same line
opening.standing_note: stock billed but not yet on a truck IS counted here — read live off the factory's own dispatch plans, not guessed at nothing. Mark 2 put it at nothing and said so; this is the real pile
opening.backlog_basis: orders that were already on the book before today and that the order reader has not walked back to yet. It reads low until the reader is walked backwards over the older order numbers

storage_cap.what_it_does: no run may be longer than the room left in the godown. The room left is the godown limit minus what is physically in there — goods finished and waiting, plus everything already billed and still waiting for a truck. It is worked out again every morning and comes down litre for litre as the day is filled, so when it reaches nothing the plant stops for the day whatever hours, bottles and orders are left
storage_cap.days_throttled_say: the days that OPENED with the godown nearly full. A day that opens with room and fills it is not counted here — it is counted in the days it bit

storage_cap.why_it_is_a_build_choice: Gurvinder ruled the godown limit and Daman declared the figure, but neither said what the planner should DO when the plan reaches it. Capping every run to the room left is the build's answer, not a ruling he gave — so it is a build choice (B20) and he can overrule it
storage_cap.headline: The godown limit is what governs this plan. It held production back on 21 of the 22 working days left, the month reaches 28.3% of the sheet, and 58 of the 84 products on the sheet are never made at all. None of that is a machine running slowly or a bottle missing — it is that there is nowhere to put what would be filled

top_binder.name: the godown is full — no room for another bottle today

day1_blocked.note: 'attempts' = how many times the planner tried and was stopped, not how many products — quote products. One product can be short of oil and packing at once, so the per-type counts can overlap. A full godown is one of the reasons: the machine had the hours and the material was there, and there was nowhere to put what it would fill

They are COUNTED as available here. If Daman rules that non-moving means unusable, every one of those codes goes to zero and blocks its whole product.

packaging room(s) not read this cycle — no live answer, no last-good, no carry: GP-FG. A room only just added to the list is NOT YET READ, not unavailable — it fills in on the next hourly cycle, and it is never a reason to refuse the whole plan. Until then packaging on hand is a FLOOR by whatever they hold, and a missing room understates stock, which is the direction that invents a stock-out.

raw-material room(s) not read this cycle — no live answer, no last-good, no carry: BH-GJ. A room that has only just been added to the list is NOT YET READ, not unavailable: it fills in on the next hourly cycle. Until then, drummed oil in it is invisible to this plan.

SF0000009 REFINED CANOLA OIL 15 KG TIN: 3,249 PCS in BH-LO — the item name says 15 kg a tin, so that is roughly 48.7 TONNES of canola sitting in the raw-material store as FINISHED TINS. It is NOT converted to litres and NOT counted anywhere in this plan: a pack size read off an item name is not a measurement, and this file does not invent litres. 1,595,702 L of EXIM oil is under loading or still in contract and is NOT booked as arriving — only trucks already on the way are

1,295,022 L is booked to arrive from OPEN BULK POs (contract quantity minus what has been drawn down). JIVO's oil POs are BLANKET orders drawn down over many part-loads — the adapter says so itself — so this is the undrawn balance of a contract, NOT a shipment on its way. It is the loosest number in this freeze and it makes oil look more available than it is.

rulebook.night_say: 10.5 hour(s) of second-shift work in the whole of the rest of the month, on 2 night(s). A second session is opened only where a machine has work it can still put somewhere

money.basis: what today's filling is worth: litres on the plan times the price each product sells for. The target and the floor are the plant's own, read from the rulebook
money.booked_basis: booked_today is goods receipts into BH-PF dated today. The receipt date lags the production date by 0-1 day and varies by SKU — this is production BOOKED, not 'produced today'.
money.mtd_basis: goods receipts per item for every day already gone this month (ji.jivo.in, factory_history.booked_by_item), pieces x litres per piece x realise. The MES sees about two-thirds of the plant; the receipts see the rest, so this is the fuller count.

month.note: the floor and the target are DAILY rules, and this is the whole month against them: 2 of 22 working days left keep the floor and 2 reach the target. Today is one day, and it is the one day the godown still has room in it — read the month, not the tick

definitions.material: the planner tried to fill it today and something it is made from ran out. The litres beside it are what it tried to fill TODAY
definitions.storage: the planner tried to fill it today, the machine had hours and the material was there — and there was no room left in the godown to put it. The godown holds 827,000 L and it is full of goods that are already sold and waiting for a truck, so nothing more can be made until something leaves the gate. No purchase order fixes this one. The litres beside it are what the planner tried to fill TODAY
definitions.no_order: nobody has asked for it TODAY — it is in the month's target, and the litres beside it are that whole month's line, not today's want. 2 of these are really ordered, just for a later day — nobody is waiting on them yet, so they are marked and not counted as unwanted. 18 of them nobody has ordered at all — they are only expected
definitions.no_line_time: somebody has really ordered it and the plan did not get to it today — every machine that can fill them was full. The godown was also too full to fill more than can be sent out. The litres beside it are that product's whole month on the sheet
